item.research_question: Does the mere increase in the number of constituent elements in high entropy alloys (HEAs) lead to sluggish grain boundary diffusion, and how does the nature of added constituents affect diffusion kinetics compared to pure metals and binary alloys?
item.material_system: CoCrFeNi (quaternary) and CoCrFeMnNi (quinary) high entropy alloys with equiatomic proportions
item.processing_route: Arc melting of 99.99 wt.% purity solid pieces in equiatomic proportions, re-melted 4–5 times for homogeneity, followed by homogenization at 1473 K for 50 h; samples cut to 8 mm diameter and 1 mm thickness, mechanically polished, and subjected to diffusion annealing at 673 K, 723 K, 873 K, 1073 K, and 1173 K
item.test_conditions: Radiotracer analysis using 63Ni isotope (68 keV β-decays) deposited on sample surfaces; annealing in quartz tubes under 5 N purified Ar atmosphere; serial sectioning with 0.3 μm thickness for low-temperature measurements; grain size >250 μm; absence of elemental segregation confirmed by Atom Probe Tomography (APT) at 60 K
key_findings: Grain boundary width (δ) estimated at approximately 0.5 nm for both alloys, consistent with FCC metals.
Grain boundary energies estimated at 0.8–0.9 J/m² and found to increase significantly with temperature, more pronounced in CoCrFeMnNi.
Ni GB diffusion in CoCrFeMnNi is slower than in CoCrFeNi below 800 K, but the trend reverses at higher temperatures.
Ni GB diffusion in CoCrFeNi is slower by only an order of magnitude compared to pure Ni and binary Fe-Ni alloys.
CoCrFeMnNi exhibits the largest activation energy for both GB and bulk tracer diffusion of Ni among the studied systems.
A cross-over temperature (Tc) of 800 K exists for GB diffusion, below which CoCrFeMnNi is slower and above which it is faster than CoCrFeNi.
The segregation factor (s) for Ni at grain boundaries is approximately unity, confirmed by APT showing no elemental segregation.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the cross-over behavior and diffusion rates to two opposing effects of Mn addition: (i) an increase in the average negative enthalpy of mixing (from -3 kJ/mol in CoCrFeNi to -4.25 kJ/mol in CoCrFeMnNi) which increases energy barriers, and (ii) a decrease in the melting temperature of the alloy. They argue that the chemically disordered matrix increases energy barriers in CoCrFeMnNi, while reduced diffusion entropy contributions affect CoCrFeNi, concluding that decreased diffusion is not solely a function of configurational entropy.
item.limitations: The study notes that a systematic investigation on fully characterized bicrystals is required to explain the intriguing behavior of GB energy decreasing with temperature in pure materials versus increasing in alloys, and that the exact value of GB energy is important for phase stability but requires further study.
item.future_work: The authors state that a detailed investigation of the structure and properties of grain boundaries in these HEAs would be required to explain the observed temperature coefficients of GB energy, which is beyond the scope of the present study.
quotes: Our GB diffusion measurements prove that a mere increase in number of constituent elements does not lower the diffusion rates in HEAs, but the nature of added constituents plays a more decisive role.
The segregation factor of Ni at grain boundaries in both HEAs is about unity, which completely agrees with the direct APT observations, Figs. 3 and 4;
CoCrFeMnNi shows a lower GB diffusivity than CoCrFeNi only below 800 K, the tendency, however, is reversed at higher temperatures.

System: CoCrFeNi (quaternary) and CoCrFeMnNi (quinary) high entropy alloys with equiatomic proportions. Processing: Arc melting of 99.99 wt.% purity solid pieces in equiatomic proportions, re-melted 4–5 times for homogeneity, followed by homogenization at 1473 K for 50 h; samples cut to 8 mm diameter and 1 mm thickness, mechanically polished, and subjected to diffusion annealing at 673 K, 723 K, 873 K, 1073 K, and 1173 K. Test conditions: Radiotracer analysis using 63Ni isotope (68 keV β-decays) deposited on sample surfaces; annealing in quartz tubes under 5 N purified Ar atmosphere; serial sectioning with 0.3 μm thickness for low-temperature measurements; grain size >250 μm; absence of elemental segregation confirmed by Atom Probe Tomography (APT) at 60 K. They argue that the chemically disordered matrix increases energy barriers in CoCrFeMnNi, while reduced diffusion entropy contributions affect CoCrFeNi, concluding that decreased diffusion is not solely a function of configurational entropy.. Future work: The authors state that a detailed investigation of the structure and properties of grain boundaries in these HEAs would be required to explain the observed temperature coefficients of GB energy, which is beyond the scope of the present study..
